texts.label: text
texts.orig: Scorsese's 21st feature film is adapted fromanunrepentant tell-all memoir by Jordan Belfort (played by Leonardo DiCaprio, left ), a cocksure but legally shady and morally repugnant founder of an upstart brokerage firm, who, before he was eventually brought low by an FBI investigation in the late 90s, amassed more wealth than Croesus would have known what to do with. It is an exhilarating, exhausting three-hour audiovisual bacchanalia of obscene conspicuous consumption, prostitutes and strippers, yachts and helicopters, drugs, sex and more drugs. And it is late-period Scorsese's flashiest, funniest work by some margin.
